newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil panel to meet, probably vote, on oil bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil panel to meet, probably vote, on oil bill.

text.p: A bill regulating the opening up of Brazil's oil industry to the private sector was due to be discussed and probably voted on by a committee in the Chamber of Deputies in Congress, an official said.
The committee was due to meet at 1000 local/1300 GMT Thursday, an aide to Deputy Eliseu Resende, who drew up the bill, said.

The bill, which would allow private companies to compete or enter joint ventures with state-owned oil and gas giant Petrobras, has been the subject of the last-minute discussions that have delayed the vote on several occasions.

Members of the pro-privatization Liberal Front Party spent Wednesday trying to persuade other lawmakers sitting on the committee to back a proposed amendment that would allow for a future selloff of Petrobras.
Resende's version of the legislation includes a clause which obliges the Brazilian state to maintain a controlling stake in Petrobras.
The bill would also set up a new regulator for the sector and scrap fuel price subsidies within three years.

If approved in the committee, the bill advances to the floor of the lower house. Government leaders said Wednesday they wanted to hold that vote next week. The legislation also has to be approved in Brazil's Senate.
